title: Gordon Street housing and heritage designations approved
subtitle: Also approved: Stevenson Street infill, York-Elizabeth land use changes, Lowe's Road flooding concerns, and a closed session on downtown land.
overview: Council approved a zoning amendment for a 150-unit stacked townhouse development and eight single detached homes at Gordon Street, Lowe's Road West and Dawn Avenue {{vote:m4}}. Nearby residents did not oppose the project but asked for the emergency access to move to Gordon Street and for fewer homes on Dawn Avenue. They also raised flooding, traffic and parking worries. Councilors asked staff and the developer to look again at the emergency access during site plan review, and staff said city-funded drainage upgrades on Lowe's Road are in design.

Council also approved two heritage designations over owner objections: the Hanlon farmhouse at 331 Clair Road East {{vote:m5}} and the barn and farmhouse at 2187 Gordon Street {{vote:m6}}. Staff said these designations protect the buildings from demolition and guide alterations. Staff also said the legislative deadlines left no later opportunity.

Council approved a 10-unit apartment building at 14 Stevenson Street North {{vote:m2}} and Official Plan Amendment No. 93 to implement the York-Elizabeth Land Use Study {{vote:m3}}. Before the open session, council met in closed session on downtown land at Baker Street. The mayor reported afterward that staff direction was given.

decisions.item: Gordon Street, Lowe's Road and Dawn Avenue rezoning
decisions.detail: Council approved rezoning to allow a 150-unit stacked townhouse development and eight single detached homes, and found no further public notice was needed for minor modifications {{vote:m4}}.
Council received the owner's objection and approved the designation by-law for the farmhouse {{vote:m5}}.
Council received the owner's objection and approved the designation by-law for the barn and farmhouse {{vote:m6}}.
Council approved Official Plan and zoning amendments to allow a 10-unit multi-residential building {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved City-initiated Official Plan Amendment No. 93 to put the York-Elizabeth Land Use Study designations into the Official Plan {{vote:m3}}.

debate: Delegates on the Gordon Street development said the neighbourhood had already absorbed major intensification. They asked to move the emergency access from Dawn Avenue to Gordon Street and to reduce the Dawn Avenue lots from eight to six.

Residents raised flooding on Lowe's Road, parking spillover onto a short street, and shortcut traffic. The applicant's representative said stormwater would be infiltrated on site, apart from one small existing runoff area draining to city open space. City engineering staff said it has capacity, and that Lowe's Road drainage upgrades are funded and in design.

On the emergency access, staff said Gordon Street was ruled out early because of traffic conflicts, and that Dawn Avenue helps with servicing and grading. Councilors still asked staff and the developer to look again at site plan stage. Staff also said the lot split would go to the Committee of Adjustment, which is a public process.

On heritage, staff and Heritage Guelph said the properties meet several designation criteria. Staff said council could not designate later if it declined now, and that a withdrawn designation at 331 Clair Road East would allow demolition after 2025. Councilors stressed the rarity of the stone slot barn and the few heritage buildings in the south end.
On Stevenson Street North, a councilor asked about added traffic from ten units. Staff said a traffic study is not required at that size and the impact would be small.
